blindSummary:
In October 2021 a district court in this state/province issued the country's most important trans-affirming ruling, ordering cancellation of the army's forced discharge of a transgender soldier and holding that the military should have considered her a woman when assessing fitness for duty — a landmark institutional recognition. In June 2024, after the defence ministry reversed the army's 'natural death' classification and recognised her 2021 death as service-related, the soldier was buried at the country's national cemetery, in this state/province; approximately 60 activists gathered to protest the burial, a visible public rejection of state recognition of a trans person at the national memorial ground.

The court ruling is a positive institutional signal but is historical (2021) and addresses a specific administrative-military dispute rather than establishing general protections; no continuing local legal advantage for visitors follows from it. The burial protest is traveler-facing — public hostility in an open space — but small in scale (about 60 people) and documented as non-repeating.
blindSourceSummaries: The national news agency (7 October 2021): a district court in this state/province ordered cancellation of the army's forced discharge of the deceased transgender soldier, holding that the military should have considered her a woman when reviewing fitness for duty — described as a landmark ruling in a suit brought to overturn the discharge.

A domestic outlet (25 June 2024): the transgender soldier was interred at the national cemetery in this state/province on 24 June 2024 — after the defence ministry reversed the army's original classification and recognised the 2021 death as service-related; about 60 activists gathered to protest the burial, arguing her service did not qualify her for interment there.

The national news agency (4 April 2024): a defence-ministry review committee recognised the late transgender soldier's death as an on-duty death, reversing the 'natural death' classification that had stood after her forcible discharge in January 2020; the ministry notified the bereaved family.
